summary: This week saw a mix of official momentum and persistent questions about UAP researchers. President Trump reiterated that UFO documents are coming "very soon," while the Department of Defense confirmed the White House is coordinating the release of previously unseen UAP material. Meanwhile, several deaths and disappearances of scientists connected to government research drew White House attention, though an ex-FBI agent stated the cases appear unrelated to one another. Astrophysicist Avi Loeb pushed back on sensationalism, framing UAPs as a straightforward scientific data problem, while UFO researchers pressed Trump to follow through on his disclosure commitments. The FY2026 National Defense Authorization Act UAP briefing deadline looms on June 30, setting a congressional checkpoint for continued transparency efforts.
